lines: Did you want to ask where I belong?

Until we decide together, the party is where I belong.
I'm not sure where I belong.
I wish I had a clear answer, but I don't.
Something about my allegiance is missing from my memory.
I hope time or familiar faces help me understand.
No village name feels certain when I try to remember.

Some places seem familiar, but none enough to claim.
I cannot tell whether I am lost or simply without a home.

The road behind me is as unclear as the one ahead.
If I learn the truth, I will tell you plainly.
For now, every answer feels like a guess.
I do not know whether my home is gone or merely forgotten.
That uncertainty follows me from village to village.
I am sorry. I truly do not know.
We aren't in a village right now.
There is no village around us for me to belong to.

There are no village borders here to compare with my home.
We are on the road, not in someone's settlement.

No boundary here marks a community I could join.
We should reach a settlement before you ask if it is mine.
Out here, both of us are only travelers.

I am no visitor here.
